title: Your 2027 Money Reset Checklist (8 Steps That Actually Stick)

lines.say: New year, new budget?
This year, let's set it up so it actually sticks.

lines.cap: Here's the 2027 money reset: eight things in two parts. Four you do once this week, and four that run all year.
lines.say: Here's the twenty twenty-seven money reset. Eight things, in two parts. Four you do once this week, and four that run all year.
Keep score as we go. How many can you already check off?
Part one. Set it up, this week.
Here's the list.
One. Know your take-home pay, per paycheck. Not your salary. The number that actually lands in your account.
Two. Give every bill a paycheck, and even the two checks out, so there's no broke week. That's episode one.
Three. List every cost that isn't monthly, and turn it into a small amount per paycheck. That's episode three.
Four. Find the months with three paychecks, and decide now what each extra one will do. That's episode six.
Part two. Let it run, all year.

scene.head: LET IT RUN · ALL YEAR
items: One debt target, every extra dollar

lines.say: Here's the rest.
Five. List every debt, pick snowball or avalanche, and send every extra dollar at one target. Episode two ran the numbers.
Six. Build a starter emergency fund, so one flat tire doesn't land on a credit card.
Seven. Automate it. Bills, sinking funds and savings all move on payday, without you deciding every time.
And eight. Fifteen minutes, every other Sunday. Check the balances, and adjust one thing.

scene.label: Starter emergency fund: one month of bills
scene.sub: rent, car, phone, insurance and the rest, from episode one

lines.cap: For the emergency fund, a simple first goal is one month of bills. In our example from episode one, that's $2,371.
lines.say: For the emergency fund, a simple first goal is one month of bills. In our example from episode one, that's twenty-three seventy-one.
Reach it faster by sending one of your three-paycheck months straight there.

items.t: Did every bill get paid from the right check?
What surprised me, and which fund covers it?
How much closer is the debt target?

lines.say: And the money check-in only needs three questions.
Did every bill get paid? What surprised you? And how much closer is the target?

lines.cap: So, what's your score out of eight? Put it in the comments. Zero is a perfectly good place to start.
